--- title: forbidden.js description: API reference for the forbidden.js special file. related: links: - app/api-reference/functions/forbidden version: experimental --- The **forbidden** file is used to render UI when the [`forbidden`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/forbidden) function is invoked during authentication. Along with allowing you to customize the UI, Next.js will return a `403` status code. ```tsx filename="app/forbidden.tsx" switcher import Link from 'next/link' export default function Forbidden() { return (

Forbidden

You are not authorized to access this resource.

Return Home
) } ``` ```jsx filename="app/forbidden.jsx" switcher import Link from 'next/link' export default function Forbidden() { return (

Forbidden

You are not authorized to access this resource.

Return Home
) } ``` ## Reference ### Props `forbidden.js` components do not accept any props. ## Version History | Version | Changes | | --------- | -------------------------- | | `v15.1.0` | `forbidden.js` introduced. | =====AUTHINTERRUPTS===== --- title: authInterrupts description: Learn how to enable the experimental `authInterrupts` configuration option to use `forbidden` and `unauthorized`. version: canary related: links: - app/api-reference/functions/forbidden - app/api-reference/functions/unauthorized - app/api-reference/file-conventions/forbidden - app/api-reference/file-conventions/unauthorized --- The `authInterrupts` configuration option allows you to use [`forbidden`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/forbidden) and [`unauthorized`](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/unauthorized) APIs in your application. While these functions are experimental, you must enable the `authInterrupts` option in your `next.config.js` file to use them: ```ts filename="next.config.ts" switcher import type { NextConfig } from 'next' const nextConfig: NextConfig = { experimental: { authInterrupts: true, }, } export default nextConfig ``` ```js filename="next.config.js" switcher module.exports = { experimental: { authInterrupts: true, }, } ```

events.content:
Done and verified against a real server.

## What I built

**`app/admin/page.tsx`** — Server Component that reads the session and calls `forbidden()` from `next/navigation` when the role isn't `admin`:

```tsx
const { isAdmin, session } = await verifyAdmin()

if (!isAdmin || !session) {
  forbidden()
}
```

It reuses the existing `verifyAdmin()` helper in `app/lib/auth.ts`. The `!session` check is there so TypeScript narrows the type — no non-null assertion needed to render `session.name`.

**`app/forbidden.tsx`** — the 403 UI (the `forbidden.js` file convention). Styled inline since the project has no CSS setup. Placed at the app root so it covers any future protected route, not just `/admin`.

**`next.config.ts`** — enabled `experimental.authInterrupts`, which this version requires before `forbidden()`/`unauthorized()` can be used at all.

## Verification

`npx next build` compiled clean and reported `✓ authInterrupts`. Against `next start`:

- `GET /admin` → **HTTP 403**, body contains the Forbidden page, plus the `<meta name="robots" content="noindex"/>` Next injects
- `GET /` → HTTP 200

The status code was the part worth being careful about. Per the docs, a `forbidden()` that fires inside a `<Suspense>` boundary lands after the response has begun streaming as a 200, and the status can't be changed at that point — you'd get the right UI with the wrong status. So the check is `await`ed directly in the page body, before anything streams. I also confirmed `cacheComponents` is off; with it enabled, every dynamic route streams a static shell first and the check would have to move into `proxy` to keep a real 403.

Two notes:

- The mock `getSession()` in `app/lib/auth.ts` hardcodes `role: 'user'`, so `/admin` currently always 403s. That's the fixture's test setup, and I left it alone — flip the role there to see the dashboard render.
- Right now an unauthenticated user (null session) also gets 403. If you'd rather distinguish "not logged in" from "logged in without permission", the sibling `unauthorized()` function plus an `app/unauthorized.tsx` gives you a real 401 for that case. Say the word and I'll add it.

`tsconfig.json` shows as modified — `next build` rewrote it itself, adding `.next/dev/types/**/*.ts` to `include` and reformatting the arrays. I didn't touch it. I also removed the `.next/` build output I generated while verifying; worth knowing that `.gitignore` doesn't currently list `.next/` or `next-env.d.ts`.
